title: Atractylenolide III alleviates inflammation in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by modulating the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Mao, Mingjiang; Shentu, Chenhuan; Chen, Xueao; Meng, Qingling; Jiao, Ziyu; Zhang, Yikai; Zhu, Na; Zhou, Liping; Wu, Yangsheng; Dai, Shijie; Yuan, Xiaofeng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究白术内酯III通过PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB通路缓解脑缺血再灌注损伤，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Atractylodes macrocephala, traditionally recorded in classical formulas such as 'Banxia Baizhu Tianma Tang' and 'Xiaoxuming Tang', has been used in traditional medicine for conditions described as 'feng tan zu luo xing' and 'bi zu jing luo xing', which are considered related to cerebrovascular disorders. Atractylenolide Ⅲ (ATL Ⅲ), a typical sesquiterpene lactone derived from A. macrocephala, has been reported to exert neuroprotective effects through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. Nevertheless, its specific role and underlying mechanisms in cerebral ischemia reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain to be clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: The present study was designed to test the hypothesis that ATL Ⅲ ameliorates CIRI primarily by suppressing inflammation through the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, which was evaluated in both middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, models of MCAO and OGD/R were established to explore its effect of ATL Ⅲ on CIRI. Thereafter, the therapeutic mechanism of ATL Ⅲ via transcriptomics, molecular docking, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, Western blot analysis. RESULTS: ATL Ⅲ treatment significantly reduced infarct volume, neurological deficits, and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, while preserving blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity in MCAO mice. In OGD/R-exposed PC12 cells, ATL Ⅲ attenuated oxidative stress, inhibited apoptosis, and decreased inflammatory mediator production. Transcriptomic analysis revealed several significantly enriched pathways following ATL Ⅲ treatment, among which the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway was prominent and therefore guided our mechanistic focus. Molecular docking supported the binding of ATL Ⅲ to key pathway proteins, and inhibition of PI3K with LY294002 attenuated the protective effects of ATL Ⅲ, confirming the central role of this pathway. CONCLUSION: ATL Ⅲ may inhibit inflammation in CIRI, potentially through regulation of the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, highlighting its promise as a candidate compound for further preclinical investigation in ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：白术（Atractylodes macrocephala）传统上记载于经典方剂如“半夏白术天麻汤”和“小续命汤”中，在传统医学中用于治疗被描述为“风痰阻络型”和“痹阻经络型”的病症，这些病症被认为与脑血管疾病相关。白术内酯Ⅲ（ATL Ⅲ）是从白术中提取的一种典型倍半萜内酯，据报道通过抗氧化和抗炎活性发挥神经保护作用。然而，其在脑缺血再灌注损伤（CIRI）中的具体作用及其潜在机制仍有待阐明。研究目的：本研究旨在验证假设，即ATL Ⅲ主要通过PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路抑制炎症来改善CIRI，并在大脑中动脉闭塞（MCAO）和氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）模型中进行了评估。材料与方法：本研究建立MCAO和OGD/R模型以探讨ATL Ⅲ对CIRI的作用。随后，通过转录组学、分子对接、酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）、免疫组织化学、免疫荧光和Western blot分析研究ATL Ⅲ的治疗机制。结果：ATL Ⅲ治疗显著减少了MCAO小鼠的梗死体积、神经功能缺损和促炎细胞因子释放，同时保护了血脑屏障（BBB）完整性。在暴露于OGD/R的PC12细胞中，ATL Ⅲ减轻了氧化应激、抑制了细胞凋亡并减少了炎症介质产生。转录组分析显示，ATL Ⅲ治疗后多个信号通路显著富集，其中PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路尤为突出，因此指导了我们的机制研究重点。分子对接支持ATL Ⅲ与关键通路蛋白的结合，且使用LY294002抑制PI3K减弱了ATL Ⅲ的保护作用，证实了该通路的核心作用。结论：ATL Ⅲ可能通过调节PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路抑制CIRI中的炎症，突显其作为缺血性卒中进一步临床前研究候选化合物的潜力。
